summary: Fixed Linux bundles billed by the hour at the bundle's hourly rate, capped at its monthly price; a stopped instance keeps billing at the same rate until it is deleted.

egress.included: 1 TB to 10 TB a month depending on the bundle
egress.note: Every bundle includes 1-10 TB of transfer, halved in Mumbai, Sydney, Jakarta, Malaysia, Hong Kong and Sao Paulo. Both directions count against the allowance, but only outbound traffic over it is charged. Overage runs from $0.09/GB (US, Canada, most of Europe, Hong Kong) to $0.17/GB (Sydney): Tokyo $0.14, Mumbai and Seoul $0.13, Jakarta $0.132, Singapore and Spain $0.12, Malaysia $0.108, Sao Paulo $0.15. Not priced by the calculator.

notes: Lightsail's hourly price is the monthly price divided by 744 (31 days), taken from AWS's own price list. A 730-hour month therefore bills $23.54 on the $24 bundle, and the $24 cap is only reached in a 31-day month. The calculator's monthly cap reproduces this.

A stopped instance is still billed: 'Lightsail instances and managed databases incur charges until they are deleted. These resources accrue charges even when they are in the stopped state.' Only deleting the instance ends the charge.

AWS does not publish whether a partial instance-hour is rounded up. The card bills pro-rata hours, so A (166.67 hours) costs $5.38. If each of the 1,000 ten-minute runs were billed a whole hour, A would be $32.25. This is an open question, not a modelled rule.

The bundle includes its SSD and its public IPv4 address; there is no separate disk or IP line. Extra block storage is $0.10 per allocated GB-month, attached to one instance, 8 GB to 16 TB per disk and 15 disks per instance.
IPv6-only bundles are $1.50-$4 cheaper a month ($3.50 for 0.5 GB) but cannot take a static IPv4 address. This card prices the public-IPv4 bundles.
Windows bundles cost more ($9.50-$4,204 a month) because they include a Windows Server licence. Not priced here.
Snapshots cost $0.05 per GB-month, manual and automatic. Automatic snapshots keep the latest seven daily copies and are deleted with the instance. Not in the calculator.

AWS labels memory and disk in GB; the card treats those numbers as GiB, the unit the site uses throughout. The difference is about 7% and never changes which bundle is the smallest fit at the sizes A/B/C use. All 25 Linux bundles with a public IPv4 address are listed.
Lightsail containers, managed databases, object storage, CDN distributions, load balancers and Lightsail for Research are separate products on separate meters and are not priced by this card.
